title: Standard Exceptions and Custom Error Types
learningObjectives: Explain the main rules of standard and custom exceptions.
Identify the key C++ constructs used for standard and custom exceptions.
Apply standard and custom exceptions in a small program.
Recognize common failure cases and safety concerns.
Test a practical scenario and justify the chosen approach.

understand.concept: Standard exception classes communicate failure categories: invalid_argument for unacceptable arguments, out_of_range for range violations, logic_error for violated assumptions and runtime_error for runtime failures. Custom types are useful when a caller needs distinct domain handling.
understand.whyItMatters: Exception types and diagnostic messages improve troubleshooting and allow callers to respond to different failures.

practise.guidedTask: Validate a username. Throw invalid_argument for blank input and a custom DuplicateRecord exception for a simulated duplicate. Catch and respond to each distinctly.
practise.independentTask: Design an inventory example with custom MissingProduct and InsufficientQuantity errors. Explain why standard errors alone might not be enough for caller decisions.
